key_insight: Underwater C3-JEPA learns a predictive world model for underwater ROV salvage using only synchronized multi-view RGB and control signals. It can anticipate how objects move and interact under contact and hydrodynamic lag without relying on contact sensors.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of planning and controlling near-field heavy-load underwater salvage operations, where contact dynamics are hard to sense directly and vehicle motion is delayed by water dynamics.
method: Encodes synchronized multi-camera RGB observations into object-centric latent representations.
Conditions predictions on vehicle control inputs to model how task-object state evolves over time.
Uses a cross-view, context-extended JEPA-style predictor to infer future latent state under contact interaction and hydrodynamic lag.
Operates without explicit contact sensors by learning predictive dynamics from visual and control data.
impact: This is useful for robotics and embodied AI practitioners because it shows how to build a sensor-light world model for complex underwater manipulation. It can improve forecasting, planning, and control in environments where direct measurement is unreliable or impossible.

paper_title: Underwater C3-JEPA: An Object-Centric Cross-View World Model for ROV Salvage
paper_authors: Yuncong Yang, Jinlong Li, Yulong Xue, Feng Wu, Chunwen Zhang
